points.name: Octavia E. Butler Landing
points.activity: Perseverance touched down here on February 18, 2021 after the "seven minutes of terror" descent on its sky crane. NASA named the site after science-fiction author Octavia E. Butler.
points.subtitle: Mars 2020 landing site
points.details: The rover's first parking position after landing, from the mission waypoint data.

photos.caption: Front Hazcam: the landing site in the rover's first days

points.name: Van Zyl Overlook
points.activity: Perseverance parked here to film Ingenuity's first flight at Wright Brothers Field, about 65 m away. Named after Jakob van Zyl, a JPL leader who helped make the mission possible.
points.subtitle: Rover position during Ingenuity's first flight
points.details: Rover position at the end of sol 52 (site 3, drive 2046).

points.name: Perseverance (latest position)
points.activity: Where Perseverance was at sol 2022, the latest position in this map's data, after driving 45.2 km since landing, outside the crater rim.
points.subtitle: Mars 2020 rover
points.details: Site 93, drive 0  ·  45.25 km driven

points.name: Ingenuity's final airfield (Airfield Chi)
points.activity: Ingenuity's 72nd and last flight ended here on Jan 18, 2024 (sol 1036). A rotor blade was damaged and the mission ended after 72 flights, 18.1 km and 129 minutes in the air, far beyond the 5 test flights it was built for. The team nicknamed the area Valinor Hills.
points.subtitle: Mars Helicopter Ingenuity
points.details:
Landing site of flights 67, 68, 69, 70, 71 and 72  ·  max altitude 16 m
Distance flown by then: 18.14 km

points.name: Jezero crater
points.activity: A 45-50 km crater that held a lake about 3.5 billion years ago. Rivers built a delta on its western side, and it was chosen for Perseverance because those lake and delta rocks could preserve signs of ancient life. Named after a town in Bosnia and Herzegovina; 'jezero' means 'lake'.
points.subtitle: Crater  ·  IAU name "Jezero"
points.details: Size about 47.5 km  ·  centre from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature

points.name: Neretva Vallis
points.activity: The ancient river valley that cut through the crater's western rim and fed the lake, building the delta. Perseverance explored the channel's mouth in 2024, where it found the "Cheyava Falls" rock.
points.subtitle: River valley  ·  IAU name "Neretva Vallis"
points.details: Size about 17 km  ·  centre from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature

points.name: Una Vallis
points.activity: A small valley west of Jezero, named after the Una river in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia.
points.subtitle: River valley  ·  IAU name "Una Vallis"
points.details: Size about 5 km  ·  centre from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature

points.name: Belva crater
points.activity: A 0.9 km impact crater in the western delta. Its walls expose layers of delta sediment; Perseverance photographed them from the rim in 2023. Named after a town in West Virginia, USA.
points.subtitle: Crater  ·  IAU name "Belva"
points.details: Size about 0.9 km  ·  centre from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature

points.name: Hartwell crater
points.activity: A 1.7 km impact crater on the crater floor, named after a town in Georgia, USA.
points.subtitle: Crater  ·  IAU name "Hartwell"
points.details: Size about 1.7 km  ·  centre from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature

points.name: Marysville crater

points.subtitle: Crater  ·  IAU name "Marysville"
points.details: Size about 1.85 km  ·  centre from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature
